stories.title: AI In Our Courts: Useful Or A Magic 8 Ball?
stories.ltme_summary: A columnist writing on Legal Tech Monitor comments on a Kentucky judge's handling of an AI issue, in which a police officer allegedly relied on AI facial recognition alone to pick a suspect, contrary to his department's guidelines, and the match was wrong. The judge compared blind reliance on AI to using a Magic 8 Ball. The post links to a longer piece for Above the Law.
stories.hook: A Kentucky judge likened blind reliance on AI facial recognition to using a Magic 8 Ball to pick a suspect

stories.title: 'Legal 111, how can I help?': National service funding plans ring alarm bells
stories.ltme_summary: The House of Commons justice select committee has published recommendations to overhaul what it calls a fragmented legal services sector. The first is a national legal service, modelled on NHS 111, that would signpost people to support. The committee also proposes funding sources, including an interest on lawyers' client account scheme, which the Law Society opposes as flawed. Other recommendations cover legal services regulation and civil litigation funding.
stories.hook: MPs propose a national legal service funded partly by lawyers' client account interest, drawing Law Society opposition
entities: House of Commons justice select committee

stories.title: How WSP scaled global contract management with AI-powered contract review | Agiloft
stories.ltme_summary: Agiloft, a contract lifecycle vendor, publishes a customer account of WSP's global contract management rollout. It says WSP ran a 12-week RFP, selected Agiloft, and went live over six months, starting in Latin America with about 3,000 employees before moving to Canada, the US and the UK. The account is drawn from a podcast appearance by WSP's Senior Director of Global Legal Operations and promotes the vendor's Astra AI platform.
stories.hook: Agiloft's WSP account says a global CLM rollout went live in six months

stories.title: DISCO Named ‘Access to Justice Innovation of the Year’ in 2026 LegalTech Breakthrough Awards | DISCO
stories.ltme_summary: DISCO, the litigation technology vendor, says it has been named Access to Justice Innovation of the Year in the 2026 LegalTech Breakthrough Awards. The recognition is for its AI-enabled work with Amicus ALJ, a UK-based non-profit supporting people facing capital punishment in the United States. DISCO says Amicus used its platform to review transcripts from roughly 200 capital cases, supporting Racial Justice Act claims. The award is a vendor claim based on the awards programme.
stories.hook: DISCO says its AI platform won an access to justice award for work with Amicus ALJ

stories.title: Customer Stories
stories.ltme_summary: Eve Legal's customer stories page lists case studies from US personal injury, employment, workers' compensation and social security firms using its AI platform. Headlines cite outcomes such as a time reduction for medical malpractice notices and an intake conversion rate of 60 per cent. The results are the firms' figures as the vendor presents them and are not independently checked. The extract is a page index only.
stories.hook: Eve Legal lists customer case studies claiming AI-driven gains for US plaintiff firms

stories.title: AI Maturity Index | Factor
stories.ltme_summary: Factor describes its free AI Maturity Index, a 20-topic self-assessment for law firms and in-house teams that scores AI maturity against a market benchmark. The page says results come with a recommended roadmap and that responses are checked against a scoring rubric. It is a vendor product page promoting the assessment and its paid team and individual reports.
stories.hook: Factor offers a free 20-question AI maturity assessment for law firms and legal teams

stories.title: Effortlessly connect iManage to your existing AI tools - iManage
stories.ltme_summary: iManage promotes its integrations that connect its document management platform to AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, Harvey, Legora, Claude and ChatGPT. The page says permissions, ethical walls and audit trails carry through to each tool, and describes an MCP server. It quotes several law firm and legal technology users. The page is vendor marketing, and the customer quotes are not independently verified.
stories.hook: iManage says its MCP server lets Harvey, Claude and ChatGPT work on firm documents under existing permissions

stories.title: Where to start with the SRA's AML findings: learnings with Eloise Butterworth of All Things Risk | Legl
stories.hook: Legl's webinar write-up says firms should start AML fixes with the firm-wide risk assessment

stories.title: Turning the SRA's AML Findings into Action, with All Things Risk (18 November 2026) | Legl
stories.ltme_summary: Legl promotes a webinar recording with Eloise Butterworth of All Things Risk, covering the SRA's latest AML findings and how firms can self-assess their maturity. The listing gives the session topics and the date of 18 November 2026. The form on the page did not load in the extract. It is a vendor event promotion, not an independent report.
stories.hook: Legl offers a recording of its AML webinar on acting on SRA findings

stories.title: Legal AI Decision Support: Govern It Before You Rely on It
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic publishes a guide arguing that legal AI decision support is safe only when the decision path is governed, with rules, human checkpoints and audit logs. It cites the US National Center for State Courts classing decision-support tools as high-risk, and a Stanford evaluation that found legal research tools hallucinated between 17 and 33 per cent of the time. The piece promotes Neota's control layer, so its framing is the vendor's own position.
stories.hook: Neota Logic says legal AI decision support needs governance before lawyers rely on it

stories.title: Think You Know Zebraworks? Look Again. | Zebraworks
stories.ltme_summary: nQ Zebraworks describes its expanded Revenue Acceleration features from a recent webinar, covering collections follow-up, billing accounts for complex client structures and AI-enriched financial data. It says the collections tool drafts follow-up emails for staff to review, and that a Claude-based analysis ran through its MCP server. The page is vendor promotion of its own product direction.
stories.hook: Zebraworks adds AI-drafted collections emails and an MCP server for financial data

stories.title: Smokeball | The Sell Life Member Benefit
stories.ltme_summary: Smokeball offers members of The Sell Life a 50 per cent discount on its onboarding fee for new customers. The offer covers personalised implementation, training and access to legal workflow tools. Smokeball says the terms and conditions apply and the offer is for new customers only. It is a vendor partnership promotion for its practice management software.
stories.hook: Smokeball offers 50 per cent off onboarding for members of The Sell Life

stories.title: Personalize law firm event invitations with CRM data | Vuture
stories.ltme_summary: Vuture, part of Marigold, sets out how law firms can use CRM data to target and personalise event invitations. The post advises matching contacts by practice area, industry, relationship type and engagement history, and says tailored invitations improve registration and turnout. It is a marketing guide promoting the vendor's approach rather than a report of a deployment or customer result. No figures are given in the extract.
stories.hook: Vuture argues law firms should use CRM practice and engagement data to personalise event invitations

stories.title: The Money Train — See Generally
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law's weekly roundup covers several BigLaw stories: Cravath's new salary scale from $235,000 to $440,000 with special bonuses up to $40,000, a contested domain registration tied to Cahill Gordon, a bar grievance against a US Attorney, and Simpson Thacher's recruitment of former Weil partners. It also notes Kirkland's reported free legal work for the Trump administration. The newsletter is a digest of law firm business news rather than legal technology.
stories.hook: Above the Law digest tracks Cravath pay scale and Weil partner moves across BigLaw

stories.title: European human rights court bans Romanian lawyer over AI use
stories.ltme_summary: The European Court of Human Rights has barred a Romanian lawyer from representing applicants before it for two years after finding she used AI to draft a submission citing nonexistent cases. According to the court's statement, relayed by the Law Society Gazette, the errors meant the court spent considerable time verifying the observations. The lawyer admitted the AI use and accepted she had not checked the document adequately. The court applied its Rule 44D exclusion power.
stories.hook: ECtHR bars a Romanian lawyer for two years after AI-drafted submission cited nonexistent cases

stories.title: Legora snaps up Hubspot’s Erika Fisher as chief legal officer
How to Use a VA Disability Rating Tool Before Filing Any Appeal
How Elite Litigation Boutiques Beats Cravath’s Salary Scale
stories.ltme_summary: LawFuel reports that litigation boutique Holwell Shuster & Goldberg has set a 2027 associate salary scale $5,000 to $10,000 above prevailing BigLaw rates, and matched Cravath's 2026 bonuses of up to $155,000 for senior associates. The firm announced the scale on 20 November. The article places this within a wider pay race that followed Milbank's and Cravath's moves.
stories.hook: Holwell Shuster & Goldberg sets 2027 salaries above BigLaw and matches Cravath bonuses

stories.title: Keep Legal Client Intake Details Out of Automated Marketing Briefs
Legal agentic AI and the problem of rule-bending or breaking
stories.ltme_summary: Three academics from Warwick and Queen Mary University of London argue in a Legal Futures guest post that recent reported failures of general-purpose AI models to follow rules could carry lessons for agentic AI in legal practice. The piece uses a case of a US M&A practitioner who built a personal playbook on Anthropic's Claude, and asks whether such agents can be trusted to follow professional rules. The extract is the opening section only; the full article sets out the authors' conclusions.
stories.hook: Warwick and Queen Mary academics ask whether agentic AI can be trusted to follow rules in legal practice

stories.title: AI and human rights: Sir Geoffrey consults ChatGPT
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Sir Geoffrey Vos, who has retired as Master of the Rolls, asked ChatGPT how Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights should change to protect against cyber-fakes, before his Mayflower Lecture at the University of Plymouth. Vos called the response an extraordinary essay, but said he disagreed with its proposed amendments and that the courts should decide how the right to privacy applies to AI.
stories.hook: Former Master of the Rolls Sir Geoffrey Vos tested ChatGPT on Article 8 ahead of a lecture

stories.title: Solicitors' Charity faces crisis as donations plummet
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that donations to The Solicitors' Charity made from residual client balances have halved so far this year, according to the Gazette's understanding. Unclaimed client balances made up 57 per cent of the charity's 2025 income of £1.8m. The charity's director says it may have to be less generous and make support more time-limited, and asks compliance officers to explain the drop. The story links the decline to uncertainty over the future of client accounts.
stories.hook: Solicitors' Charity says residual client balance donations have halved this year

stories.title: Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill: the industry reacts to bid to modernise ‘feudal’ system
Kim Findlow appointed as 63rd CILEX President
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Conveyancer's headline reports that Kim Findlow has been appointed as the 63rd president of CILEX. The page's teaser is an unrelated SQE item, so the appointment is taken from the headline only and the extract contains no biographical detail or start date. The appointment concerns the professional body for legal executives rather than technology.
stories.hook: Kim Findlow appointed 63rd CILEX President, according to the headline

stories.title: Diary of a High Street Conveyancer – Have a day off!?
Financial services must do more for bereaved after FCA finds communications confusing and unclear
September the highest month on record for IHT receipts
Lawtech incubator receives £3m MoJ funding to encourage AI adoption
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Wills and Probate reports that a lawtech incubator has received £3m in funding from the Ministry of Justice to encourage the adoption of AI across the legal sector. The extract is limited to a rendering of the site's standfirst and does not describe the incubator's programme, its selection process or the timing of the funding. The item sits under the publication's probate and wills coverage, so the link to that sector is likely through the incubator's work with providers serving it.
stories.hook: MoJ backs a lawtech incubator with £3m to push AI adoption across legal services

stories.title: Copilot at Microsoft Ignite: Expanding what’s possible with intelligence built for work
stories.ltme_summary: Microsoft's SharePoint and Microsoft 365 for legal blog reports Ignite 2026 announcements for Copilot, including general availability of Home, Chat and Cowork, Auto model routing and new plugins for legal and other teams. Microsoft says Work IQ draws on Microsoft 365 data and that Agent 365 is expanded. The post is Microsoft's own product announcement, and the extract does not show legal-specific features in detail.
stories.hook: Microsoft says Copilot Home and Cowork are generally available, with new legal plugins

stories.title: What AI at work really costs
stories.ltme_summary: Microsoft says research it commissioned with GigaOm finds Copilot had the lowest estimated monthly cost for everyday and advanced AI users, compared with ChatGPT Enterprise and Claude Enterprise. Microsoft quotes $30 a month for everyday use of Copilot against $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude, based on October 2026 list prices. Microsoft says quality was broadly comparable. Microsoft ran the testing itself, so the comparison is the vendor's own.
stories.hook: Microsoft-commissioned study puts Copilot cheapest of three enterprise AI tools

stories.title: Important Security Notice – Java Vulnerability
stories.ltme_summary: SOS Legal warns customers that a recently identified Java vulnerability affects parts of the infrastructure supporting its software. The company says not all installations are at risk and has published a security bulletin on how to check exposure and fix it. Customers are asked to share the guidance with their IT teams and to contact SOS Support if unsure.
stories.hook: SOS Legal warns some installations may be exposed through a Java vulnerability
